howToRegenerate: the record is hand-kept, like design/copy-duplicates.json: `npm run check:copy-contract --print-sections` prints which sections the build carries and which have no row, and `--print-hollow` prints the worklist the count is kept against. The gate never rewrites this file.
ruleOfExit: A row leaves when its section is deleted, renamed away, or promoted into another page - a row for a section the build no longer makes is contract-stale, and the gate says so. A hollow sentence leaves the worklist when it is rewritten to carry a fact a reader can use, or when a ruling settles why it stays; it is NOT kept with a status of 'fixed', because a signature in hollowRuled is an exemption and an exemption for a defect that is no longer there is itself a defect (round 7's F6: a needle that never matched its defect read as a green light).
why: Every section of a built page is a function of three inputs: the reader it is written for, what that reader can do or believe once they leave the section, and the voice register it is written in. The communication reviews priced lines of copy (rounds 6, 7, 8) and never once asked those three questions of a section, so thirty-odd rounds of line edits produced a patchwork: sentences that pass every shape rule - length, duplication, source, anchor ceiling, escapes, dated surfaces - while carrying nothing a reader can act on. This record is the missing address: it names the reader per section, and npm run check:copy-contract fails when a section has no reader, when a page addresses two readers in one voice, or when the count of sentences carrying no reader-usable fact gets longer.

vision.note: The site's one vision belongs to the author of the club, not to the delegate. The letter exists as a scaffold, and its slots stay bracketed until the author fills them (DESIGN.md's Copy rule: brackets stay until a source exists). The gate fails a letter that calls itself sent while any slot is still bracketed; an unsent letter prints and exits 0, because sending it is the operator's ask, parked with its trigger in PLAN.md §Milestones. Until the letter is sent, every row below carries settledBy naming the delegate as its author, and the rows are a draft the author corrects rather than a vision anyone owns. The author answered parts of the letter on 2026-11-19: question 1 for all five pages, question 2 for `/join` and `/chat` only, and most of question 3. Those answers are landed in the letter's slots beside their date, and the rows whose reader the letter settles now say so in `settledBy` instead of reading a blanket draft. `status` stays `unsent` because brackets remain - after `/` and `/dates` in question 2, question 4's three sentences, question 5's one sentence - and the gate fails a `sent` letter with a bracket under it.

hollow.note: set from a run: the gate counts sentences on the built body sections that carry no club fact (place, time, price, person, platform, thing to carry, a number, an action) and no path out, and fails when the count rises above this number. The number is a worklist, not a score. It went 8 -> 4 when four ruled signatures were registered, and it is **0 as of 2026-11-19 because the operator deleted the four sentences that were on it** - '/chat's "Any can be dropped mid-sentence; none is a prerequisite for arriving.", '/chat's "The channel is the live thing.", '/join's "The conversation that runs between meetings.", and '/past's cancelled-state line ('(A) drop all four of those.', **S079**, **D453**). Three of them have no replacement. '/past's notice still owes exactly one body line (DESIGN.md 'States': missing content is a state, never a blank), so that one is now generated from `closedOff`, the count the page already computes, and the detector reads its spelled number as a fact - so it is not itself a hit. This is deliberately NOT the move the record refused on 2026-11-19 morning (**D451**), when the bar stayed at 4 rather than dropping to 3: there the deleted sentence was *exempt*, so the worklist had not changed and lowering the number would have hidden a slot that was still open. Here the worklist itself is empty, so 0 is what the run printed, and the record's own rule of exit is what filled it. Consequence, stated where a future session will read it: from this commit any flagged sentence at all is a regression, and `hollow-count-worse` fires on the first one.
hollow.probe: npm run check:copy-contract --print-hollow @measured 2026-11-19 by that command, printing 'hollow sentences on the built pages: 0 (bar: 4)' against the old bar and 'PASS' with the bar re-set to 0. History the gate keeps: 8 flagged before the ruled signatures were registered, 4 after, 0 when the four remaining hits were deleted on the author's word (**S079**, **D453**)
